visual.general_description: Grayscale frontal chest radiograph showing a large rounded central opacity filling the lower thorax between the two lung fields.
visual.detailed_description: Grayscale frontal view of the chest and shoulders with the lower neck at the top edge. The laterality letter "R" and a two-digit number are printed in white at the upper left, and a small white pictogram of a person appears at the upper right corner. Both clavicles, scapulae and the ribs are visible, and both lung fields appear dark. A large rounded bright opacity occupies the central and lower thorax, widest in its lower part, and merges inferiorly with the bright upper abdomen so that the diaphragm contours and the costophrenic angles are not distinctly seen. The right lung base ends in a rounded dark margin against this opacity. The left lung field is visible mainly in its upper and middle parts. Soft-tissue shadows of the lateral lower chest wall are visible on both sides. No other text, arrows or measurement marks are visible.

visual.general_description: Coronal CT section of the chest in which the bright heart is surrounded by a wide band of uniform intermediate-gray material.
visual.detailed_description: Black-and-white coronal-plane cross-section of the chest with a black border on all sides. The two lung fields are black in the upper chest. The heart chambers and the great vessels in the centre are very bright, and the vessels at the thoracic inlet and the ribs seen in cross-section along both lateral margins are also bright. A wide band of uniform intermediate-gray material encircles the bright heart, thickest toward the right of the image and along the lower border of the heart, and is separated from the lungs and the large homogeneous gray organ at the lower left of the image. Smaller gray soft-tissue structures lie at the bottom centre and lower right. No text, side markers, arrows or measurement marks are visible.
